title: Grusch files IG complaint and names witnesses

tellings.quote: I filed my complaint. I told them who to interview. And, you know, they ultimately were like, Holy shit, this is credible.
I made them get interviewed by the inspector general because we're crossing our T's here because this shit is crazy.
tellings.difference: This telling adds that he vetted nearly 40 sources over about 2019-2022 and made them sit for IG interviews to be thorough, but it leaves out the IG's reaction that the complaint was credible.
tellings.link_reason: Both are Grusch's firsthand account of pointing the DoD Inspector General to his witnesses so they could be interviewed as part of his complaint. The core event is the same: he sent his sources to the IG.

as_told.title: Grusch brought 40 witnesses; complaint found urgent and credible

plain: A whistleblower named David Grusch says that in 2022 he filed a complaint with an inspector general, a government watchdog office, and told its investigators whom to interview, and that they came back saying, in his words, "Holy shit, this is credible." He tells Michels he vetted his sources over several years and made them sit for interviews with the inspector general themselves "because this shit is crazy." On the show the number is given as about 40: Michels calls them people "who have handled exotic UFO material firsthand" and names the intelligence community's inspector general, while a former Pentagon official named Luis Elizondo insists the testimony is not all secondhand. If true, dozens of insiders went on record with an official watchdog about hidden UFO material.
